name: Community Engagement and Restoration Mini Grant
summary: Small rolling grants of up to $5,000 for local groups in Maryland and the West Virginia part of the Chesapeake watershed to run projects such as tree plantings, rain gardens and stream cleanups.

geography.label: Maryland and the Chesapeake Bay watershed portion of West Virginia

steps: Online application, at least eight weeks before project start

eligibility.rule: At most 3 Trust awards excluding sponsorships and Corps awards, or first Trust reapplication in at least 8 years
Project is still to be completed
Work is voluntary, or goes beyond permit, decree, mitigation or enforcement requirements
Has separate people for Executive Officer and Project Leader
Has an EIN and, for a West Virginia project, a SAM Unique Entity ID
Neither the Executive Officer nor the Project Leader is associated with a for-profit entity

documents: Site plan and project design for planting projects
Detailed maintenance plan for planting projects
Native plant list for planting or restoration
Landowner permission letter for planting on property the applicant does not own or on private property
Commitment letters from collaborators who have committed to the project
Knowledge objectives for projects with outreach components
Evaluation plan for projects with outreach components
Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement, if held, for West Virginia projects

applicant_types.quote: Who can apply: Nonprofit organizations, community associations, faith-based organizations and more.

geography.quote: Eligible Locations: Maryland and the Chesapeake Bay Watershed portion of West Virginia

access.quote: The Chesapeake Bay Trust's grant applications are all submitted through an online system

window.quote: Deadline: Rolling basis. Requests are accepted on an on-going basis until funds are fully expended for the fiscal year.

amount.quote: How much can be awarded: Up to $5,000.

co_finance_required.quote: Match is encouraged, but not required.

effort.quote: The Chesapeake Bay Trust's grant applications are all submitted through an online system, using the "Start a New Application" button below.
please send your application to us at least eight weeks before your project starts.
All projects are evaluated by technical experts.

eligibility.quote: This program is open to applicants that have received less than four awards (i.e., received three or fewer awards) from the Trust. Applicants who have received four or more awards from the Trust but are re-applying to the Trust for the first time in eight or more years are eligible to apply. Sponsorships and Chesapeake Conservation Corps awards are not counted toward the eligibility cap.
Are already completed. We cannot provide reimbursement funding;

Are required by a Federal, state, or locally issued permit, decree, mitigation, or enforcement action. In some cases, the Trust may elect to fund optional portions of required projects that go “above and beyond” the regulatory requirements.
Both an Executive Officer and a Project Leader, two separate individuals, must be identified for all applications.
type, mission, EIN number, and SAM UEI number (if applying for a project in West Virginia).
individuals associated with for-profit entities cannot serve in either role, but can be engaged in the project as contractors or partners.

after_award.quote: If approved, the Trust will send an award agreement with award conditions and due dates of status, progress, and final reports.

documents.quote: All planting projects must include a plant list, site plan, project design, photos of the site where planting/restoration is proposed, and a detailed maintenance plan.
List of native plants that will be used in the planting/restoration project in the application.

For projects planned on properties other than that of the applicant and/or private property, attach a letter of commitment stating that permission has been granted by the entity owning the land on which the project will be completed.
